title: E2E-WAVE: End-to-End Learned Waveform Generation for Underwater Video Multicasting.
abstract: We present E2E-WAVE, the first end-to-end learned waveform generation system for underwater video multicasting. Acoustic channels exhibit $20-46 \%$ bit error rates where forward error correction becomes counterproductive—LDPC increases rather than decreases errors beyond its decoding threshold. E2E-WAVE addresses this by embedding semantic similarity directly into physical layer waveforms: when decoding errors are unavoidable, the system preferentially selects semantically similar tokens rather than arbitrary corruption. Combining VideoGPT tokenization ($1024 \times$ compression) with a trainable waveform bank and fully differentiable OFDM transmission, E2E-WAVE achieves $\boldsymbol{+} \mathbf{5 ~ d B}(\mathbf{1 9. 2 6 \%})$ PSNR and $\boldsymbol{+} \mathbf{0. 1 0}(\mathbf{1 4. 2 8 \%})$ SSIM over the strongest FEC-protected baseline in less challenging underwater channel (NOF1) while delivering real-time 16 FPS video at $128 \times 128$ resolution over 2.3 kbps channels-impossible for conventional digital modulation. The performance gap only increases in harsher channels (BCH1, NCS1). Trained on a single channel, E2E-WAVE generalizes to unseen underwater environments without retraining, while HEVC fails at sub-5 kbps rates and SoftCast’s AWGN assumptions collapse on frequencyselective channels.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Look Once, Beam Twice: Camera-Primed Real-Time Double-Directional mmWave Beam Management for Vehicular Connectivity.
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequencies promise multi-gigabit connectivity for vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks, but face challenges in terms of severe path loss and mobility-related beam misalignment. Reliable V2X connectivity requires fast, double-directional beam alignment. However, existing methods suffer from high training overhead and limited generalization to unseen scenarios. This paper presents VIsion-based BEamforming (VIBE), a hybrid model-based, closed-loop, learning architecture for real-time double-directional mmWave beam management primed by camera sensing. VIBE fuses machine learning, model-based reasoning, and closed-loop RF feedback to balance beam-pair establishment latency with link quality. VIBE bypasses exhaustive training overhead and accelerates link establishment by leveraging camera observations to reduce the beamsearch space. Lightweight beam refinement and offset tracking mechanisms adaptively refine beams in response to dynamic application requirements. VIBE is implemented and evaluated across online indoor/outdoor testbeds, public datasets, and realtime vehicular experiments, demonstrating strong generalization capabilities, making it suitable for real-time V2X communication. Comparisons with 5G NR hierarchical beamforming show that VIBE consistently maintains lower outage rates. Furthermore, VIBE outperforms state-of-the-art end-to-end ML models for beam selection when evaluated on public datasets and achieves outage rates as low as $1.1-1.4 \%$. The results show that a hybrid model-based, closed-loop learning architecture is better suited for real-world mmWave vehicular connectivity than end-to-end trained ML models. For reproducibility, we publish our code to https://github.com/UNL-CPN-Lab/Look-Once-Beam-Twice.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: ORBIT: Meta-Learned Online Convex Optimization for Low-Latency In-Orbit Computing.
abstract: As Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations transition into distributed in-orbit computing platforms, the transport layer has emerged as a critical bottleneck. Existing protocols fail to account for the extreme energy-coupled nonstationarity of LEO links, where capacity can fluctuate dramatically within a few RTTs due to orbital dynamics and finite battery headroom during eclipse periods. This triggers a vicious cycle of packet losses and power-hungry retransmissions that can lead to satellite brownouts. This paper introduces ORBIT, a metalearned online convex optimization (OCO) framework designed for low-latency in-orbit computing. ORBIT treats congestion window selection as a proactive optimization problem, consuming real-time physics-based telemetry to predict link capacity and energy availability. We propose a novel meta-learned Follow-The-Regularized-Leader (FTRL) algorithm that pre-learns the geometry of the orbital optimization landscape from historical traces, enabling rapid adaptation with minimal computational overhead. To handle prediction uncertainty, we further introduce ORBIT-U, a robust variant that incorporates confidence radii into the optimization loop. Evaluations on a production-scale LEO emulator demonstrate that ORBIT achieves significant overall latency reduction compared to BBR, with substantial improvements during active connection periods, all while maintaining high throughput and constellation-scale memory efficiency. This work demonstrates that physics-informed meta-learning can transform LEO network constraints into structured optimization opportunities for future space-based edge clouds.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Fine-Grained Indoor Occupancy Estimation with Sparse Passive WiFi Sensing Data.
abstract: Indoor occupancy monitoring constitutes a cornerstone of modern building management yet faces significant implementation challenges in complex environments. While passive WiFi sensing offers a privacy-preserving and cost-effective solution, its efficacy is severely compromised in indoor environments characterized by low occupant density. Unlike outdoor scenarios where high traffic volumes compensate for intermittent probe transmissions, indoor settings suffer from aggregate data scarcity, which renders traditional outdoor-centric methods ineffective regarding accuracy and stability. To address these limitations, WIOM is proposed as a deep learning framework that reformulates occupancy estimation as a spatiotemporal reconstruction problem. First, the Cross-Attention and SpatioTemporal Reconstruction (CASTR) network leverages stable fixed-address patterns to rectify randomized signal noise and bridge temporal gaps. Second, a multi-objective adaptive loss balances pixellevel fidelity with global counting consistency to ensure robust convergence under sparse supervision. Third, the SpatioTemporal Median Filter (STMF) suppresses transient fluctuations caused by device irregularities. Experimental evaluations in a controlled indoor environment demonstrate that WIOM effectively recovers fine-grained occupancy dynamics from sparse inputs, achieving state-of-the-art performance with improvements of 68.3% in counting accuracy and 64.7% in stability compared to existing baselines.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: TorBinPack: Topology-Aware Online Scheduler for Minimizing Congestion in AI Superclusters.
abstract: The exponential growth in Large Language Model (LLM) training has created unprecedented network congestion challenges in AI supercluster environments. Modern distributed training generates massive inter-accelerator communication that overwhelms traditional scheduling approaches, leading to severe throughput degradation in multi-tenant clusters. We present TorBinPack, a machine learning-enhanced topology-aware scheduler that adaptively optimizes job placement to minimize network congestion. TorBinPack introduces the Throughput Congestion Index (TCI) to quantify network contention across concurrent distributed training jobs and combines least squares regression with conflict-aware placement optimization, prioritizing intra-ToR allocation to minimize cross-rack traffic. Extensive tracedriven evaluations on three production-derived supercluster topologies demonstrate that TorBinPack reduces network congestion by $55.2 \%$ compared to state-of-the-art schedulers while maintaining low scheduling overhead, achieving up to $27 \%$ reduction in job waiting time.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: WiSLAT: A Simultaneous Device Localization and Target Tracking Method for Wi-Fi Systems.
abstract: It has been shown that the channel state information (CSI) of a Wi-Fi system can be exploited to localize Wi-Fi devices or track trajectory of a moving target. In the existing literature, both sensing tasks are treated separately and some prior information is usually requested, including the signal fingerprints, the locations of some anchor devices in the Wi-Fi system, etc. In the proposed WiSLAT method, however, it is shown that both sensing tasks can assist each other, such that the request on prior system information can be eliminated. Particularly, in a Wi-Fi system with an access point (AP) and at least three stations, where the locations of the stations are unknown, the WiSLAT is designed to detect the Doppler frequencies of the downlink CSI at the stations, such that their locations and the trajectory of the target with respect to the AP can be inferred. The joint detection can be conducted by searching the optimal stations’ locations and target’s trajectory, such that their corresponding Doppler frequencies fit the observed ones best. Due to the tremendous non-convex search space, a low-complexity sub-optimal algorithm integrating alternate optimization, extended Kalman filter and density-based clustering is proposed in WiSLAT. Experiments conducted in indoor environments demonstrate the effectiveness of WiSLAT, achieving a median trajectory-tracking error of 0.68 m.

title: DualEngine: A Thermal-Aware Vision Inference Framework via Mobile and Cloud Co-Execution.
abstract: On-device AI enables real-time inference on mobile devices but often suffers from thermal throttling due to CPU/GPU overheating. Offloaded AI, which delegates inference tasks to nearby edge servers, has emerged as a promising alternative, yet the thermal impact of the wireless modem is largely overlooked. In this paper, we conduct a thermal analysis of both on-device AI and offloaded AI, revealing that (i) modem heat becomes significant during offloading and is thermally coupled with processor temperature, and (ii) coordinated co-execution of ondevice AI and offloaded AI can improve FPS and thermal stability over standalone modes. Building upon these insights, we present DualEngine, a thermal-aware co-execution framework that dynamically allocates thermal budgets between processors and modem. Leveraging reinforcement learning, DualEngine adjusts the DNN model selection, CPU/GPU clock frequency, and offloading rate to prevent thermal throttling while maximizing inference performance. Implemented on COTS smartphones and an edge server, DualEngine shows up to $12.75 \times$ improvement in thermal constraint compliance and $3.69 \times$ increase in FPS under realistic and dynamic environments.

title: Augmented Communication Reliability for UHF RFID Systems via Polar-Coded EPCs.
abstract: Ultra-High Frequency (UHF) RFID systems have emerged as a cornerstone for the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). Despite their wide adoption and transformative impact across industries, they still suffer from significant reliability challenges in noisy environments, due to limited power budget and susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. In this paper, we propose an Augmented Reliability (AR) framework that enhances RFID communication reliability without requiring hardware or protocol modifications. Our approach leverages polar codes—a capacity-achieving error-correction technique—to embed redundancy directly into standard EPC packets. To ensure backward compatibility with existing RFID deployments, the framework introduces two novel mechanisms: (1) EPC Tunneling, which encapsulates polar-coded EPCs (PolarEPCs) in unused tag memory to create a protected “tunnel” for original EPC bits, and (2) EPC Routing, which dynamically retrieves the rater-optimal PolarEPC variant from user memory to adapt real-time channel conditions. Together, these mechanisms achieve near-optimal performance across varying signal-to-noise ratios while maintaining full compliance with the EPC Gen2 standard. Evaluation results show that the AR framework achieves a ${1 5. 8 \%}$ increase in throughput and a ${5 4. 6 \%}$ reduction in latency compared to conventional RFID networking solutions. This augmented reliability further translates into a series of system-level cascading benefits, including a $23.5 \%$ increase in maximum communication range, a $13.4 \%$ improvement in liquid penetration, and a ${2 5. 9}{\%}$ enhancement in motion resilience.

title: An Air-Sea Collaborative Computing Method for Open-Sea USVs based on UAV-Assisted Communications and USV Clusters.
abstract: Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) play a crucial role in maritime surveillance, resource exploration, and disaster response. However, their communication range and computing capabilities are limited, which causes data transmission delay and an inability to execute complex computing tasks. Existing studies focus on local computing or small-scale USV collaborative computing, but they suffer from insufficient resource pooling and ineffective computing capabilities for dependent tasks. To address these issues, this paper proposes an air-sea collaborative computing method for open-sea USVs. Specifically, we first propose a USV clustering mechanism to group USVs dynamically to better organize their computing resources. Secondly, we construct an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted multi-hop link model to enable stable data transmission among USV clusters. Based on this, we construct an air-sea collaborative computing model that uses latency and energy as objectives and considers task dependency, maximum tolerable delay, resource capacity limits of USV clusters, and UAV relays as constraints. Finally, we improve the multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm by integrating cluster-aware state representation and dynamic resource allocation mechanisms, and use it to solve the proposed model. Simulation results show that the proposed model outperforms baseline methods significantly in terms of latency, energy, and task completion rate.

title: BFI-Fall: Learning Beamforming Feedback Information in Wi-Fi Sensing for Fall Detection.
abstract: Indoor fall detection is a core technology for smart healthcare. The practical deployment of traditional Channel State Information (CSI) solutions is significantly hindered by their reliance on firmware modifications. In this paper, we propose BFI-Fall, an efficient sensing system for fall detection, leveraging Beamforming Feedback Information (BFI) from standard MultiUser Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MU-MIMO) protocols. Our system extracts features directly from standard communication traffic without hardware customization, offering inherent commercial compatibility. To overcome the inherent quantization noise in BFI signals, we design a deep learning framework that integrates a 2D-CNN for spatial feature extraction, a BiLSTM for temporal modeling, and a Self-Attention mechanism for key feature capture. Ablation studies demonstrate that the 2D-CNN boosts the recall rate to 95.8%, while the attention mechanism further reduces the False Negative Rate (FNR) significantly to 1.9%. This study demonstrates the viability of BFI for building reliable fall detection systems and provides a novel perspective for the design of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems.

title: Poster: Overcoming Probabilistic Quantum Repeaters with TESQR.
abstract: We present the Transduction-Enabled Superconducting Quantum Repeater (TESQR), a hybrid architecture for long-distance entanglement distribution that replaces probabilistic optical Bell-state measurements (BSMs) with high-fidelity superconducting quantum processing. By converting optical photons to microwave photons at the repeater node and performing gate-based entanglement swapping on superconducting qubits, TESQR guarantees a final entangled state at every trial. Under realistic noise models and fiber losses, we demonstrate end-to-end fidelities above 0.5 at 40 km total distance, with average and peak improvements of 63% and 159%, respectively, in entanglement distribution rates over purely photonic counterparts.

title: Poster: Q-RISE: Entanglement Routing Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: Quantum entanglement routing in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks faces critical challenges from dynamic topology, decoherence and limited quantum resources. We propose Quantum entanglement Routing with Integrated Selection and Enhancement strategy (Q-RISE), an optimisation algorithm that jointly addresses fidelity thresholds, communication delays and resource consumption under coherence time constraints. QRISE integrates a Markov-enhanced Cascaded Swap Fidelity Model (MCSFM) for accurate fidelity estimation and a Minimum Purification Rounds (MPR) mechanism for resource-efficient entanglement enhancement. Simulation results demonstrate that QRISE outperforms Q-CAST, the strongest baseline, by reducing average waiting time by up to $46 \%$, decreasing quantum resource utilisation by up to $67 \%$ and maintaining high end-to-end (E2E) fidelity in networks of up to 90 nodes. These results confirm QRISE as a scalable and reliable entanglement routing solution for future quantum LEO satellite constellations.

title: POSTER: A Dataset Construction Framework for Detecting MitM Attacks on the 5G N3 Interface.
abstract: Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks against the $\mathbf{5 G}$ User Plane (UP) remain underexplored, despite the central role of the N3 interface in transporting user traffic between the Radio Access Network (RAN) and the User Plane Function (UPF). In particular, GTP-U forwarding over UDP exposes the user plane to packet interception, manipulation, replay, and denial-of-service conditions when an adversary gains a privileged position in the transport infrastructure or compromises key network functions. At the same time, publicly available intrusion-detection datasets do not adequately represent $\mathbf{5 G}$-native traffic, and none captures the specific protocol structure and attack surface of the N3 interface. This poster presents a methodology for constructing an ad hoc 5G security dataset for MitM detection on the UP. The approach combines replayed benign traffic, controlled attack injection within a 5 G testbed, and packet-level feature extraction from tunneled GTP-U traffic. The resulting dataset is intended to support future machine-learning-based detection of MitM activity in realistic 5 G environments.

title: Agentic AI with Emulation-assisted Prevalidation for Edge-Cloud Service Orchestration.
abstract: Autonomous service orchestration under the sixthgeneration (6 G) edge-cloud networks requires intelligent decisionmaking while overcoming Quality of Service (QoS) violations. However, general-purpose agentic frameworks learn through trial-and-error on production infrastructure, creating unacceptable risks for mission-critical 6 G use cases. We present AgentEdge, a multi-agent orchestration framework that uses emulation to validate all LLM-based planning decisions before execution. AgentEdge achieves $2.76 \times$ higher success rates than ReAct baselines across six orchestration scenarios with three state-of-the-art LLMs. AgentEdge maintains $\mathbf{4} \boldsymbol{\times}$ better API efficiency with consistent behavior, while ablation studies confirm emulation’s critical contribution ($1.47 \times$ improvement), and scales from 8 to 35 nodes with up to 300.8 W energy savings.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: LLM-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning for Task Offloading in Collaborative Edge Computing.
abstract: Collaborative edge computing uses edge nodes in different locations to execute tasks, necessitating dynamic task offloading decisions to maintain low latency and high reliability, especially under unpredictable node failures. Although deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for task offloading, DRL often suffers from high sample inefficiency and local optima, whereas LLMs struggle with real-time decision-making. To address these limitations, we propose LeDRL, a hybrid decision framework that couples a lightweight LLM with self-attention-enhanced DRL for real-time task offloading. LeDRL constructs structured, context-aware prompts capturing node status, task semantics, and link dynamics to derive high-level strategy priors. These are selectively processed by a self-attention-based alignment module for context-aware policy optimization. A reflective evaluator distills semantic feedback from past trajectories to guide future prompts, enabling more informative and temporally generalizable LLM queries. Extensive experiments show that LeDRL outperforms baselines in task success rate, convergence speed, and real-time responsiveness across diverse network scales, achieving over 17% improvement in success rate. Furthermore, we deploy LeDRL on Jetson-based edge devices using our prototype system CoEdgeSys, demonstrating its robustness and feasibility under resource constraints. Our code is available at:https://github.com/GalleyG5/LeDRL.git.

title: Poster: TTC-Mamba: Continuous-Time Link Prediction in Opportunistic Networks via Spatio-Temporal Synergistic State Space Models.
abstract: Opportunistic Networks (OppNets) exhibit sparse, bursty contacts and long-range dependencies, making continuous-time link prediction challenging. Snapshot-based methods lose fine-grained temporal information, while Transformer-based models suffer from quadratic complexity and weak topo-temporal coupling. We propose Tri-Path Topo-Temporal Coupled Mamba (TTC-Mamba), a continuous-time spatio-temporal framework based on State Space Models (SSMs). TTC-Mamba models node history, edge intervals, and structural evolution through three complementary paths, with discretized SSMs enabling linear-complexity sequence modeling in $O(L)$. Experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate strong overall performance, improving AP on sparse Hyccups from 0.9088 to 0.9790 over TGN.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: RFpH: A Robust Water pH Assessment System Based on RFID Technology.
abstract: Water pH assessment plays a crucial role across various domains. Traditional methods suffer from low resolution, inefficiency, and are susceptible to environmental factors. In this paper, we introduce RFpH, a robust water pH assessment system implemented on a versatile Radio Frequency (RF) sensing platform, which enables seamless Received Signal Strength (RSS) and phase extraction from the backscattered signal. RFpH exploits the coupling effect between the water and the RFID tag, which inherently manifests in the backscattered signals. We conquer a series of practical challenges that typically hinder accurate water $\mathbf{p H}$ assessment. To mitigate the environmental interference, we implement a dual-tag differential scheme that fully compatible with the sensing platform, which intentionally circumvents complex circuit and advanced algorithm. To mitigate the influence of container orientation, we adopt a one-transmitter-two-receiver system architecture and leverage their geometric relationship to effectively isolate the container orientation effect from the water coupling effect. Finally, we employ a compensation method to alleviate the impact of water level variations on the backscattered signal. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that RFpH achieves robust water pH assessment with an error of less than $2.15 \%$.

title: Lightweight Dynamic Global Filter Network for Efficient Image Analysis on Edge Devices.
abstract: The deployment of deep neural networks (DNNs) on resource-constrained edge devices demands a rigorous tradeoff among inference accuracy, latency, and energy efficiency. While recent architectural innovations like Global Filter Networks (GFNet) offer efficient frequency-domain token mixing, deploying them on embedded platforms remains challenging due to static computational graphs that fail to adapt to varying input complexity. To address this, we propose EAE, a holistic Efficient image Analysis framework for Edge devices that synergizes spectral-domain model compression with a hardwareaware dynamic inference mechanism. First, we introduce a novel frequency-domain knowledge distillation technique that regularizes student feature norms and orientations against a teacher network, achieving significant parameter reduction while preserving global receptive fields. Second, we dismantle the “exit-at-every-layer” paradigm common in dynamic networks, which we demonstrate creates prohibitive synchronization overheads for lightweight backbones. Instead, EAE employs a strategic, interval-based exit placement optimized for the specific latency characteristics of embedded GPUs. Furthermore, we propose a heterogeneous orchestration strategy that offloads lightweight gating and uncertainty estimation to the CPU, thereby minimizing GPU kernel interruptions. Extensive experiments on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and AGX Orin platforms across three standard benchmarks demonstrate that EAE achieves an average inference speedup of $1.62 \times$ and $19.9 \%$ energy savings compared to state-of-the-art dynamic networks, with gains extending to $1.96 \times$ and $59.3 \%$ against the vanilla GFNet, all while maintaining competitive accuracy. Our code and dataset will be released at: https://github.com/GG-Bond-Ultra/EAE.

title: Channel-Adaptive Physical Layer Neural-enhanced Encoding for Concurrent LPWANs.
abstract: Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs) show great potential for enabling long-range, low-power connectivity for Internet of Things (IoT) devices. However, their scalability is often limited by frequent packet collisions. Previous approaches struggle to maintain robust performance across diverse channel conditions. We present PNLoRa, the first neuralenhanced, channel-adaptive physical layer encoding framework for LPWANs. PNLoRa models the real-world process of collision decoding using a custom neural encoder, enabling each transmitter (Tx) to use the waveform most suited to its channel condition. Specifically, the encoder jointly shapes the waveforms of all concurrent Txs such that, when decoding a target Tx, interference from other signals is spread evenly across the spectrum, thereby minimizing its impact on the target signal. This collision-aware, channel-adaptive design enables PNLoRa to support more concurrent transmissions across the network. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PNLoRa achieves a $3 \times$ improvement in network concurrency compared to state-of-theart solutions.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Design and Analysis of Chirp-Layered Superposition Coding for LoRa.
abstract: This paper investigates the design of chirp-layered superposition coding for LoRa, where an additional waveform is linearly superposed on a standard LoRa transmission with minimal impact on the LoRa demodulation process. We first show that any non-zero superposed signal perturbs the output of the standard dechirp-and-DFT demodulator, and then characterize the class of superposed waveforms that minimize this degradation under a given power budget. In particular, we show that a high spreading factor (high-SF) LoRa waveform superposed on a lowSF signal (e.g., SF12 on SF7) can be designed so that its impact on the standard LoRa demodulation remains small. As a result, within each low-SF symbol interval, the high-SF segment can be treated as a quasi-narrowband carrier that conveys an additional BPSK stream. We derive analytical error-rate expressions for both the low-SF LoRa layer and the superposed high-SF layer, and validate them through Monte Carlo simulations. The proposed chirp-layered superposition coding scheme improves the spectral efficiency of LoRa-based links and uses a relatively simple transceiver architecture.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Ballet in Sky: Online Satellite Downlink with Joint ISL Balancing and GS Selection under Uncertainty.
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Earth Observation (EO) satellites generate massive data but encounter significant downlink challenges due to a fundamental imbalance between uneven data distributions and fluctuating downlink opportunities. This issue is critically exacerbated by uncertain Satellite-to-GS Link (SGL) quality. To tackle the complex scheduling under uncertainty, we first propose FlowDance, a performance-guaranteed approximation algorithm for the oracle case with known SGL quality, by jointly optimizing ISL data balancing and GS group selection. We achieve this through a novel network flow model that captures the trade-off between balancing duration and downlink opportunity. Building on this, we design Ballet, a novel online learning framework. It develops a partition-batch-based exploration policy to estimate SGL qualities, which serve as the input for the exploitation process, i.e., leveraging FlowDance to guide the downlink scheduling. We provide a theoretical analysis for Ballet and verify its performance through extensive simulations using real-world satellites and GS deployment data. The results show that Ballet significantly enhances data downlink throughput compared to state-of-the-art methods, with an average improvement of at least $29.8 \%$.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: FastSET: Fast Sequential Retraining to Accelerate Real-Time Online Adaptation for Neural Receivers.
abstract: Neural receivers for wireless communication must adapt rapidly to time-varying channels to ensure reliable performance. However, frequent online adaptation incurs significant latency and computational overhead, limiting real-time deployment. Inspired by the modular design of conventional receivers, we propose FastSET, a fast sequential retraining strategy that decomposes the neural receiver into a neural estimator and a neural demapper, accelerating adaptation via a decoupled twostage sequential update. An offline model search identifies an efficient estimator-demapper split that balances performance and complexity. During online operation, FastSET first updates the estimator with a few gradient steps, then refines the demapper while keeping the estimator frozen, mitigating the inherent moving-target problem and reducing total adaptation time. We evaluate FastSET on a frequency-domain OFDM receiver under 3GPP TDL channel models and ray-traced urban scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that FastSET achieves $\mathbf{5. 1}-\mathbf{5. 9} \times$ faster adaptation than end-to-end retraining, while limiting BER degradation to within 3% compared to the baseline across diverse dynamic environments.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: DRShield: Coordinating Line-Rate Enforcement and Global Adaptation for Dynamic DDoS Defense.
abstract: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks pose a persistent threat to network availability, ranging from massive single-vector floods to sophisticated, multi-vector campaigns that dynamically shift attack patterns. Existing solutions face an impossible triangle: switch-native heuristics offer line-rate speed but lack global coordination, while centralized controllers provide optimization but suffer from architectural latency gaps, struggling to adapt to complex or rapidly mutating threats. To bridge this gap, we present DRShield, a hybrid defense framework that harmonizes the speed of programmable hardware with the adaptability of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). DRShield adopts a Two-Tier Control Loop: a Fast Loop in the data plane executes pre-compiled inference logic at line rate for immediate suppression, while a Slow Loop in the control plane performs Runtime Model Reconfiguration to strategically tune parameters. To master the joint optimization of defense resources, we propose a Graph Policy Optimization (GPO) agent that leverages Structural Awareness to identify congestion sources globally. We implement a functional prototype using Mininet emulation and validate the hardware feasibility on Intel Tofino1. Evaluation results demonstrate that DRShield is highly robust: it achieves over $98.9 \%$ goodput across a spectrum of attack scenarios, including real-world traffic replays and dynamic hybrid attacks. Crucially, it converges to effective policies significantly faster than traditional optimization methods while reducing flow table resource occupancy by $50 \%$ compared to static allocation baselines, proving that intelligent coordination enhances defense efficiency against both routine and advanced threats.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: CoMeT-Net: Consensus Memory Template Network for Real-time Traffic Anomaly Detection.
abstract: Real-time anomaly detection in Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN) demands high accuracy, low false alarms, and computational efficiency for resource-constrained edge deployment. Traditional methods struggle with computational overhead, inconsistent cross-domain performance, and suboptimal feature representations that miss subtle attacks on O-RAN's open interfaces. We present CoMeT-Net (Consensus Memory Template Network), a framework achieving state-of-the-art detection through three innovations: (1) structured memory banks enabling template-based consensus voting with $O(N \cdot C)$ complexity; (2) adaptive gating that downweights ambiguous features as a learned noise filter; (3) contrastive alignment unifying feature learning and classification. Deployed in O-RAN infrastructure via edge servers and Near-RT RIC xApp, CoMeT-Net enables dynamic threat mitigation through PRB throttling and RRC connection release. On network traffic datasets, CoMeT-Net achieves 99.35% F1 score with 10$\times$ lower false alarm rates than baselines while maintaining 0.3-3ms inference across hardware tiers from servers to Raspberry Pi 4. O-RAN testbed validation demonstrates effective isolation, degrading attacker latency to >1400ms while preserving 15-20ms for legitimate users.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: HiLo-MAE: Efficient Pre-trained Traffic Representation for Encrypted Network Sensing.
abstract: Pervasive encryption has fundamentally reshaped modern communication networks, reducing the effectiveness of traditional payload-based traffic analysis and elevating encrypted traffic classification into a core network sensing challenge. Accurate identification of encrypted traffic types is important for network monitoring, security enforcement, and resource management, yet it remains difficult due to the loss of semantic visibility and the diversity of network behaviors across applications and devices. In this paper, we introduce Hilo-MAE, an efficient pre-training framework that captures hierarchical local-global dependencies in encrypted flow data. From a networking perspective, encrypted traffic exhibits multi-scale patterns within the flow prefix, where fine-grained local byte/packet patterns and coarse-grained flow-level context jointly determine traffic semantics. HiLo-MAE leverages a Hierarchical Local-Global (HiLo) attention mechanism within a masked autoencoder architecture to model these complementary patterns, enabling robust flow representations under encryption. We evaluate HiLo-MAE on seven encrypted traffic datasets spanning enterprise, mobile, and IoT network scenarios. Experimental results show that HiLo-MAE consistently outperforms the evaluated baselines, achieving improvements of up to $26.5 \%$ in classification accuracy over the strongest compared method while maintaining favorable computational efficiency. Results across multiple benchmark datasets and few-shot settings further suggest that the learned representation can reduce reliance on large labeled datasets, making HiLo-MAE a promising candidate for scalable deployment in real-world network monitoring systems.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: WirelessSenseLLM: Zero-Shot Human Activity Understanding by Bridging Wireless Signals and Human Language.
abstract: There is a growing interest in enabling wireless sensing systems to interpret human motion from unsegmented wireless signals; however, existing CSI-based applications rely heavily on accurate signal segmentation and predefined action labels, which limit their applicability in zero-shot scenarios. We present WirelessSenseLLM, a language-driven framework that leverages large language models (LLMs)to enable zero-shot human motion understanding from unsegmented Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI). To bridge the modality gap between time-series CSI and discrete language representations, we introduce a CSI-to-Language Adapter and a cross-modal projection mechanism that allows the CSI feature to be mapped into a language-aligned semantic space. This design enables the generation of fine-grained natural language descriptions of sequential and overlapping human motions, supporting down-stream reasoning without segmented training data. We address two core technical challenges: modality mismatch between CSI features and language embeddings, and overlapping actions in unsegmented CSI streams. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong performance in zero-shot action understanding ($92 \%$ accuracy and $91 \% \mathrm{~F} 1$-score), language-based reasoning quality ($30 \%$ factual and $15 \%$ reasoning improvements), and multi-person motion explanation with an average $12.33 \%$ improvement over prior methods. These results highlight WirelessSenseLLM’s effectiveness for robust, interpretable human motion understanding from CSI signals.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: LUCID: Lightweight Unsupervised In-Network Drift Detection and Selective Update Framework.
abstract: Recent advances in programmable data planes (PDPs) have enabled the realization of in-network intelligence (INI), where machine learning models are directly executed within network switches. However, most existing INI systems assume static data distributions, overlooking concept drift, the temporal and contextual evolution of network traffic that leads to degraded inference accuracy and unreliable long-term performance. Although periodic retraining can mitigate drift, it introduces significant computational and communication overhead, especially without precise drift detection. To address this challenge, we propose LUCID, a lightweight unsupervised drift detection and selective update framework that operates entirely within programmable switches. LUCID monitors centroid deviations at decision tree (DT) leaf nodes to detect drift in real-time without relying on floating point or stateful computations, and it employs an anchor rule-based selective update to refresh only unstable rules rather than retraining the entire model. Tested on a software programmable switch, LUCID demonstrates effective drift detection with 77.0% improvement in accuracy and efficient model update 44.5% reduction in retraining overhead.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Minimizing Sensor-Cloud Resource Makespan via Low-Coupling Request Scheduling for Embedded Edge Systems.
abstract: Coupling conflicts in sensor-cloud environments become particularly severe when concurrent user demands compete for a limited pool of physical resources. Most existing cloudand edge-oriented scheduling approaches are built on assumptions of request independence and one-to-one allocation, which limits their ability to handle multi-user coupling effects arising from shared-resource competition. In this work, we formalize the scheduling problem and establish its NP-hardness via a polynomial-time reduction from the Partition problem. To tackle this challenge, we develop a low-coupling edge scheduling scheme that integrates dual-buffer queue management with an improved Kuhn-Munkres (KM) matching strategy. The method adaptively consolidates redundant service requests and computes nearoptimal request-resource mappings with a time complexity of $\mathbf{O}\left(n^{3}\right)$ and an approximation ratio of $\mathbf{O}(\ln m)$, where m denotes the number of requests. Extensive experiments on a real testbed further demonstrate consistent reductions in scheduling delay and improvements in resource utilization when compared with representative baseline methods. These results demonstrate the proposed approach’s capability to effectively alleviate couplinginduced performance degradation in sensor-cloud systems.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: Dynamic Scheduling of Dependency-Aware DAG Tasks in Cooperative Multi-Edge Computing.
abstract: With the rapid growth of data volume and stringent latency requirements in IoT applications, efficient task processing in cooperative multi-edge systems becomes increasingly critical. This paper investigates the online scheduling and offloading of dependency-constrained DAG tasks in cooperative multi-edge systems to minimize the long-term average makespan, and proves the problem is NP-hard. To address this challenge, we propose DRL-TCES, an online cooperative scheduling framework that dynamically selects cooperative edge servers via a Top-k sampling based DQN and determines workload partition ratios through completion-time balancing while jointly considering transmission, queuing, and computation overheads. Simulation results show that DRL-TCES outperforms strong baselines in makespan reduction and exhibits superior scalability and robustness.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Blind LoRa Signal Separation in Multi-Source Collisions Using Deep Neural Networks.
abstract: Collisions among LoRa packets are common in dense low-power wide-area networks and remain a key bottleneck for reliability and capacity. While existing multi-packet reception schemes can decode overlapped LoRa frames at gateways, they typically rely on preambles, known PHY parameters, or reception diversity, and rarely provide blind waveform-level separation from raw I/Q samples. This paper investigates blind separation of two simultaneously active LoRa sources at a dual-antenna receiver, which can be instantiated as a multi-antenna gateway, a testbed node, or a USRP-based spectrum monitor. Using a USRP B210, we collect 2400 real indoor/outdoor two-source collision samples under four source-array distances $(5 \mathrm{~m}, 10 \mathrm{~m}, 15 \mathrm{~m}$ and 20 m) and three angle-of-arrival separations ($30^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}$ and 60°). We formulate a dual-channel complex STFT-domain mixing model and propose a lightweight multi-channel ResNet masking network that exploits both CSS time-frequency structure and inter-antenna phase cues, trained end-to-end with permutation invariant training (PIT). On 240 held-out mixtures, the proposed separator achieves 17.4 dB mean SI-SDR and 1.72% mean pseudo-SER, comparable to a U-Net baseline and more robust than Conv-TasNet at very low SNR. Across input SNR from -10 dB to 15 dB, the model maintains pseudo-SER around 2% once SNR $\geq 0 \mathrm{~dB}$, suggesting its potential as a practical physicallayer collision recovery module for LoRa gateways, testbeds, and spectrum monitors.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: DiSC2: Bandwidth-Efficient Distributed Semantic Communication for Cross-Modal Redundancy Suppression in the Internet of Bodies.
abstract: The Internet of Bodies (IoB) requires efficient transmission of correlated physiological signals under strict bandwidth constraints. We propose DiSC2, a bandwidth-efficient distributed semantic communication framework for cross-modal redundancy suppression, which combines distributed semantic encoders, cloud-side cross-modal attention, a hybrid task-anddistortion loss, and a lightweight quantization-aware edge encoder. Unlike independent waveform transmission, DiSC2 prioritizes complementary task-relevant information across modalities and shifts redundancy exploitation to the cloud. Experiments on PttPPG and ScientISST MOVE show that DiSC2 preserves downstream classification performance more effectively than SSC and DWT+LDPC baselines, especially under low-SNR and low-CBR conditions, while remaining suitable for resource-constrained wearable sensing.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: CD-NOMA: Correlation Domain Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access for Underwater Acoustic Network.
abstract: Reliable and efficient underwater communication is essential for Underwater Internet of Things (UW IoT) applications, yet the underwater acoustic channel poses severe challenges. Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) has emerged as a promising technique that allows multiple users to share the same time-frequency resources through power-domain multiplexing and advanced signal separation. This work proposes a novel uplink multiuser framework, termed Correlation-Domain NonOrthogonal Multiple Access (CD-NOMA), for underwater acoustic networks. CD-NOMA enables simultaneous transmissions from multiple transmitters to a single receiver by exploiting the correlation properties of Zero-Correlation-Zone (ZCZ) sequences at the Physical (PHY) layer and the non-orthogonal multiplexing principle at the Medium Access Control (MAC) layer. A hybrid noncoherent decoder combining Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) with joint sequence optimization is further developed, using phase-invariant correlation metrics and complex leastsquares refinement. Emulation and experiment results demonstrate that CD-NOMA achieves superior transmission reliability.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: UniChirp: Unwrapping In-Chirp Phase Misalignment for Weak LoRa Signal Demodulation.
abstract: LoRa is widely adopted in low-power wide-area networks (LPWANs) for long-range and energy-efficient IoT communications, yet its demodulation performance degrades severely in challenging deployment scenarios with extremely low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), such as obstructed or industrial environments. A key limiting factor is in-chirp phase misalignment, which prevents coherent energy aggregation in conventional FFT-based LoRa demodulation and leads to weak spectral peaks. In this paper, we present UniChirp, a practical LoRa demodulation framework that improves robustness under weak-signal conditions by explicitly addressing the in-chirp phase misalignment. UniChirp derives a lightweight analytical model that captures chirp phase deviations induced by hardware offsets and modulation artifacts, enabling deterministic packet-level phase-prior construction without exhaustive search. Building on this model, the framework incorporates a preamble-guided phase-prior-based candidate decoding mechanism together with a structure-aware spectral filtering strategy to enhance symbollevel energy aggregation. The proposed method is implemented entirely in software and requires no modifications to existing LoRa end devices or protocol stacks. We deployed the system in real industrial production environments, addressing weak signal issues caused by environmental occlusions. Extensive evaluations using commercial LoRa hardware across controlled experiments demonstrate that UniChirp enhances symbol-level decoding robustness, achieving a $\mathbf{1. 3 ~ d B}$ improvement in SNR sensitivity over current state-of-the-art approaches.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: WiWildLoc: WiFi-based Outdoor Human Location via Beamforming Feedback.
abstract: High-precision location in unstructured outdoor environments remains constrained by the physical complexities of the wild. Under a dense canopy, the Global Positioning System (GPS) fails to provide reliable coordinates, whereas existing radio-frequency sensing is often limited by the restrictive hardware dependencies of Channel State Information (CSI). We propose WiWildLoc, a system that uses the protocol-compatible Beamforming Feedback Matrix (BFM) to achieve device-free positioning using standard commercial hardware. To recover spatial details from compressed BFM data, we design a multimodal Siamese network that decouples spatio-temporal and angular features, yielding robust fingerprints that withstand severe multipath fading. Field evaluations in bamboo groves and highdensity forests demonstrate a mean positioning error of 0.191 m and an angular MAE of 7.84°. These results provide a scalable foundation for forestry inspection and field rescue, addressing the terminal precision gap in understory environments.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: MTNTD-SLM: A Small Language Model for Malicious Traffic Detection Based on Multi-Teacher Debate-Distillation.
abstract: Malicious traffic detection on edge devices faces difficulties such as encrypted and heterogeneous traffic, rapidly evolving attack patterns, and stringent constraints on computation and latency. Existing lightweight models suffer from insufficient knowledge coverage, and single-teacher distillation fails to fully transfer the reasoning capability of Network Traffic Large Language Models (NT-LLMs). The core challenge is how to achieve the detection accuracy, generalization and interaction ability of NT-LLMs in a lightweight model suitable for on-device deployment, for which no mature solution exists yet. This paper proposes MTNTD-SLM: a Multi-Teacher Network Traffic Debate-Distillation Small Language Model. It integrates complementary knowledge from TrafficLLM, TrafficGPT and DoLLM, generates consistent labels and structured reasoning grounds, and supports knowledge distillation for lightweight models. Experiments show that MTNTD-SLM achieves $96.40\%$ F1-score on CSTNET 2023, $99.56 \%$ on USTC-TFC 2016, and reduces inference latency to only 12 ms. The study reveals that the performance ceiling of Network Traffic Small Language Models (NT-SLMs) is determined not by model size, but by the availability of unified, high-quality multi-teacher reasoning knowledge.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: FlexAttNC: A Flexible Attention-Driven Network Coding for Dynamic Wireless Networks.
abstract: Dynamic wireless networks (e.g., fluctuating link qualities and rapidly changing topologies), such as mobile ad hoc and multi-hop wireless systems, face significant challenges in reliable data delivery. Despite the prevalence of Random Linear Network Coding (RLNC), its adaptability in dynamic networks remains limited. Furthermore, existing deep neural network-based network coding methods fail to effectively adapt to dynamic channels and topologies, while often incurring long inference times, which may limit their applicability in real-time and resource-constrained environments. To address these limitations, we propose FlexAttNC, an attention-driven network coding approach augmented with a Path Feature Caching (PFC) mechanism. FlexAttNC employs a shared multilayer perceptron (MLP) within its attention mechanism to generate adaptive coding coefficients, capturing path-level heterogeneity while enhancing generalization across varying network conditions. By reusing cached path features to avoid redundant computations, PFC helps reduce inference time, enabling more efficient network coding decisions. Extensive simulations under diverse dynamic network settings show that FlexAttNC achieves a $6.5 \%$ increase in decoding probability, a $57.5 \%$ reduction in coding overhead, and an average $19.5 \%$ faster inference. Testbed evaluations further validate these results, demonstrating the practical feasibility of FlexAttNC on resource-constrained platforms.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: A Software-Defined Cost-Aware Load-Balancing Wi-Fi Mesh Network with Multiple Cellular-Enabled Gateways.
abstract: Wi-Fi mesh networks are attractive for large-scale wireless coverage, but their scalability is limited by reliance on a few wired gateways and high multi-hop forwarding overhead. Cellular-enabled Wi-Fi mesh networks with multiple gateways improve deployment flexibility, but existing solutions still suffer from rigid gateway selection, unbalanced cellular data usage, and disrupted connectivity during station (STA) mobility. We propose an software defined network (SDN) inspired, costaware load-balancing system for multi-gateway cellular Wi-Fi mesh networks. Our quadratic programming load-balancing (QPLB) algorithm jointly optimizes cellular data usage and multi-hop forwarding cost for adaptive gateway selection, and is implemented on commodity Linux-based routers. Results show $\mathbf{5 8} \boldsymbol{\%} \mathbf{- 8 3 \%}$ lower cellular quota imbalance, $\mathbf{3 4 \%}$ lower median byte-weighted hop count than greedy and equal-split baselines.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: FPFA: Flexible Polarization Fingerprint Authentication Framework for Large-Scale Devices.
abstract: Polarization Fingerprint (PF) enables cost-effective device authentication in resource-constrained IoT environments. However, its performance with a monolithic classifier deteriorates in large-scale device sets. Therefore, we propose the Flexible Polarization Fingerprint Authentication Framework (FPFA). This framework partitions the N-device set into smaller, mutually exclusive, variable-scale subsets and routes each PF sample to its dedicated sub-classifier. FPFA’s novelty lies in its configurable decomposition strategies, tailored to different requirements for accuracy, security, and computational efficiency, thereby ensuring flexibility across diverse priorities. To this end, we design and implement three policies: (1) ID-Policy, maximizing authentication accuracy for registered devices; (2) Feature-Policy, tailored for high-security needs against attacks; (3) Hybrid-Policy, blending ID and PF features to balance security and accuracy. Furthermore, we propose Class-Adaptive Networks (CANet), allowing sub-classifiers to dynamically adapt their architectures to the scale of assigned subsets. Experiments on 5,000 devices demonstrate that FPFA effectively mitigates performance degradation compared to a monolithic classifier. Notably, our policies excel in distinct metrics: ID-Policy achieves the highest accuracy; Feature-Policy offers the best security by yielding the lowest FAR while maintaining the same FRR; Hybrid-Policy strikes a balanced performance. Architecturally, adopting CANet in FPFA effectively optimizes the trade-off between computational efficiency and performance.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: Probe to Stay Fresh: Enhancing Age of Information in Energy-Harvesting Random Access Networks.
abstract: This paper investigates channel probing and reservation to optimize the Age of Information (AoI) in energyharvesting (EH) random access networks. To mitigate collisions while coping with stochastic energy arrivals, we propose a hybrid framework where nodes expend minimal energy to “probe” the channel. If probing fails, we evaluate three strategies: strict avoid free competition (SAFC), reserved nodes competition (RUC), and all-active nodes competition (AUC). We derive closed-form expressions for the network-average AoI under these three schemes and validate the accuracy of our theoretical derivations through simulations. Surprisingly, the AUC scheme consistently achieves the lowest AoI. By allowing contention after reservation failure, AUC effectively amortizes probing costs and reduces energy accumulation latency. Furthermore, we demonstrate that probing-based access significantly outperforms EH-slotted ALOHA in energy-constrained regimes, even with signaling overhead, identifying it as a superior approach for enhancing information freshness.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: Hybrid Frequency Crossover for Multi-Scale Field Reconstruction in Wireless Sensor Networks.
abstract: Environmental field reconstruction in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) is constrained by sparse and irregular sampling, limited energy budgets, and strong spatial coupling. Under these conditions, optimization-based inversion must capture both large-scale trends and localized variations, while conventional spatial-domain crossovers often entangle updates across scales. Hybrid Frequency Crossover (HFC) addresses this issue by performing recombination in the discrete cosine transform (DCT) domain, where coarse spectral structure can be inherited from one parent and finer detail from another. We instantiate this idea as HFC-2D for WSN field inversion and further extend it as HFC-X-Integrated for structure-aware general optimization through block-local spectral mixing. Results show lower reconstruction error and smoother convergence on WSN inversion, with additional competitive performance on the CEC 2017 benchmark suite (CEC2017) for structured and coupled functions.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Energy-Efficient and Queue-Stable UAV Trajectory Control via Lyapunov-Guided MAPPO with Dynamics-Aware Modeling.
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) has emerged as a promising paradigm but faces significant challenges in dynamic environments. Existing approaches face two critical challenges: jointly optimizing hybrid continuous-discrete actions yields intractable non-convex problems, while Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods lack stability guarantees and often neglect UAV mechanical dynamics, leading to suboptimal performance. To address these limitations, we propose Lya-MAPPO, integrating dynamics-aware modeling (capturing acceleration-propulsion coupling and velocity-induced interference) with hierarchical control: upper-level Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) learns trajectories, while lower-level Lyapunov scheduling ensures resource allocation with stability-aware control. The scheduler derives decisions from drift-plus-penalty bounds, providing principled guidance to balance throughput, energy, and queue stability. Extensive simulations demonstrate $98.6 \%$ queue backlog reduction versus Pure MAPPO and $17.7 \%$ energy efficiency improvement over dynamics-unaware models, achieving competitive throughput with bounded queues and low energy consumption.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: RangeTag: Adaptive Ultra-Wideband Ranging for Energy Cost-Accuracy Trade-Off in Wearable Systems.
abstract: The availability of low-cost, low-power UltraWideband (UWB) ranging radios in the past decade has enabled applications that can benefit from accurate distance time-series measurements. These applications benefit from UWB accurate wireless ranging capability, which is robust in both indoor and outdoor environments. However, adopting UWB technology in constrained wearable systems requires confronting the challenge of high radio power consumption. We present the design of a wrist-worn wearable system that combines UWB two-way ranging with Bluetooth Low Energy and an ultra-low power accelerometer to achieve high ranging accuracy while consuming significantly less power than a UWB-only ranging solution. In this work, we focus on applications that require measuring human-to-human or human-to-object distance time-series over long time intervals. For such continuous ranging applications with specific energy efficiency requirements, we demonstrate that the average UWB power consumption can be minimized by using an adaptive UWB ranging policy learned through reinforcement learning. We evaluate our design with a new hardware prototype, RangeTag, which is based on the Qorvo DWM1001 module. Our design enables energy cost and ranging accuracy trade-offs for various applications. Our evaluation shows that, for a range of ultra-low power scenarios, ranging accuracy can be improved by 20% to 40% on average compared to UWB alone.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: InterAngle: Turning Radar Interference into Beyond-Resolution Angle Estimates.
abstract: Recently, the availability of low-cost commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) millimeter-wave (mmWave) radars has accelerated their widespread adoption across diverse applications. Their compact size and high range resolution make them suitable as onboard sensors for autonomous vehicles, robots, and drones. However, their limited number of antennas constrains the angular resolution, degrading localization performance in cluttered environments. Moreover, dense deployment of on-device mmWave radars often suffers from non-negligible mutual interference, leading to ghost targets and measurement artifacts. While interference is typically regarded as a challenge, InterAngle leverages the temporal and spatial sparsity of line-of-sight (LoS) interference to enable accurate inter-device angle of arrival (AoA) estimation, even at sub-resolution angular separations and in the presence of strong environmental reflections. By addressing the practical challenges of generating, detecting, and exploiting interference signals, InterAngle unlocks new sensing opportunities beyond the AoA estimation. Our method reduces the target radar’s AoA estimation error from 7.71° to 1.31° at sub-resolution angular separations, and from 12.16° to 1.00° with strong surrounding reflections.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: Beyond RTT: Enhancing Routing Path Inference for Overlay Networks with Clock Offset.
abstract: Inferring routing paths in overlay networks is challenging because overlay encapsulation hides physical paths from tools like traceroute, while end-to-end metrics such as round-trip time (RTT) alone are insufficient for reliable inference. We propose leveraging clock offsets alongside RTTs as a two-dimensional latency space, and formulate a latency consistency condition over node triplets to infer routing paths in overlay networks. A noiseadaptive threshold is introduced to tolerate measurement noise and ensure robust inference. Evaluations via simulations, testbed emulations, and real-world cloud deployments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Adaptive Detrending-Based Channel Decoupling for Robust RF Fingerprint Identification Using CSI.
abstract: Recently, radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) leveraging intrinsic hardware characteristics of transmitted signals has become one of the most popular physical-layer authentication. In this paper, we develop a robust channel state information (CSI)-based RFFI system for identifying commercial mobile devices to further enhance the up-layer security level. The issue of channel decoupling is well addressed by adaptive trend estimation and removal or suppressing low-frequency components in the raw CSI. Due to the adaptive characteristics of multi-window trend weighting (MTW) algorithm, the former is more desirable. RF fingerprints (RFFs) are separated from the raw CSI amplitude and phase, and then fused as a hybrid representation through attention-based feature fusion. Furthermore, a multitask learning-aided framework is developed to overcome the shift of RFF feature distribution by adversarial training. We carried out extensive real-world experiments to validate the effectiveness on identifying smartphones. Experimental results suggest that our proposed scheme outperforms five state-of-the-art solutions with $\mathbf{2 . 8 7 \% - 1 8 . 8 8 \%}$ identification accuracy improvement. Using our improved framework, the accuracy can be increased by $2.70 \%- 22.91 \%$ under long-term evaluation if one dynamic dataset in the deployment phase is available to fine-tune the pre-trained model.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: RF-THERMO: Empowering Robust Wireless Temperature Sensing Under Motion Scenarios.
abstract: Wireless temperature sensing (TS) plays a key role in our daily lives. Recent work has shown the advantages of RFID-based TS (RTS), due to its ability of item-level TS. However, existing RTS works still face a fundamental limitation: temperature-induced signal variations are severely disrupted by motion interference. Using a reference tag could be a solution, but it introduces extra costs and cannot leverage existing tags widely used in IoT environments. In this work, we present RF-Thermo, an RTS system that can work under motion interference with one single tag. The key insight is that by selecting two appropriate frequencies, the tag can respond similarly to motion but differently to temperature, allowing multiple frequencies to filter out motion interference while preserving temperature information. To provide multiple frequencies and improve time efficiency, we use the OFDM technique and tackle challenges like subcarrier synchronization. We also demonstrate that unstable RF transceivers cause random phase offset (RPO), leading to significant TS errors. By modeling the physical layer ON/OFF state signal, we correct RPO and extract motion-free temperature fingerprints. Finally, we propose ThermoNet which adopts a triplet network to increase the distinguishability between similar temperature fingerprints and thus improve the sensing precision. Extensive experiments show that RF-Thermo achieves an accuracy within $2.3^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in both static and dynamic scenarios, which outperforms the current SOTA RTS methods.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: CODA: A Continuous Online Evolve Framework for Deploying HAR Sensing Systems.
abstract: In always-on HAR deployments, model accuracy erodes silently as domain shift accumulates over time. Addressing this challenge requires moving beyond one-off updates toward instance-driven adaptation from streaming data. However, continuous adaptation exposes a fundamental tension: systems must selectively learn from informative instances while actively forgetting obsolete ones under long-term, non-stationary drift. To address them, we propose CODA, a continuous online adaptation framework for mobile sensing. CODA introduces two synergistic components: (i) Cache-based Selective Assimilation, which prioritizes informative instances likely to enhance system performance under sparse supervision, and (ii) an Adaptive Temporal Retention Strategy, which enables the system to gradually forget obsolete instances as sensing conditions evolve. By treating adaptation as a principled cache evolution rather than parameter-heavy retraining, CODA maintains high accuracy without model reconfiguration. We conduct extensive evaluations on four heterogeneous datasets spanning phone, watch, and multi-sensor configurations. Results demonstrate that CODA consistently outperforms one-off adaptation under non-stationary drift, remains robust against imperfect feedback, and incurs negligible on-device latency.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: CADRE: Card-Agnostic Domain-Aligned RF Embeddings for Virtual PIN Pads on Passive NFC Cards.
abstract: Near Field Communication (NFC) cards are widely used for identification, but their passive nature often limits the ability to incorporate additional security mechanisms. As a result, anyone holding the card may be incorrectly recognized as an authenticated user. To overcome this limitation, this paper presents a secure manual password input framework using a virtual PIN pad for passive NFC cards. Users input passwords by pressing designated regions on the card, which induces measurable impedance variations in the NFC antenna. These variations change the RF signals subtly, and a deep learning model is used to infer the intended password from the resulting signal patterns. A key challenge is that identical press interactions can produce significantly different responses across NFC cards, which yields unreliable recognition. To address this, we introduce a lightweight recognition approach that operates directly within the RF feature space at the penultimate layer of a temporal neural encoder. An adversarial domain-alignment module reshapes virtual PIN pad press-response embeddings into compact, card-invariant clusters, which enables stable and consistent recognition across heterogeneous cards. To support model training and evaluation, a reconfigurable software-defined radio (SDR) testbed is developed, and PIN pad press-response data are collected from commercially available ISO/IEC 15693 cards. Recognition is performed using a Mahalanobis distance metric derived from a calibration-based covariance model that captures feature correlations. Experimental results show that the proposed system achieves a 98.20% recognition acceptance rate and remains robust under substantial noise degradation. The framework is fully card-agnostic and can be seamlessly integrated into existing NFC infrastructures.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: FBRoT: Transforming Flash Memory into Root of Trust for IoT Terminals.
abstract: With the popularity of IoT applications, their security has become a focus of academic and industrial attention. Root of trust (RoT) may ensure that only the correct image can be loaded onto to to mitigate the risk of malicious code intrusion. However, existing RoT solutions for the IoT terminals usually require the introduction of additional specific hardware. This does not meet the stringent size, cost, and power requirements of IoT terminal. In addition, some IoT terminals may be used for leasing, which requires their RoT to be able to be updated by the tenant. Existing RoT does not address the issue well. Therefore, this paper proposes an approach to build a RoT for IoT terminals using flash memory, named FBRoT. FBRoT implements the RoT security functions based on the computing power of NAND flash FTL (Flash translation layer). NAND flash is a versatile component for IoT terminals and usually used to store system image. Flash read and write operations for image loading must be performed by the FTL. So, the security functions of RoT cannot be bypassed easily. As a compute unit independent of the host device, FBRoT may isolate the potential malicious attacks from the host effectively. Since the implementation is based on reusing flash’s inherent computing power, FBRoT does not need to introduce specialized security hardware. We have also designed a secure RoT update mechanism for FBRoT, which may make different IoT terminal tenants to build their own proprietary trust chains. Evaluation of the FBRoT prototype system shows that FBRoT incurs reasonable overhead, making it a practical security solution for resource-constrained IoT terminals.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: FlexiView: Flexible Video Quality and Playout Optimization for Mobile Video Streaming.
abstract: The increasing demand for mobile video streaming presents a significant challenge in delivering high-quality, uninterrupted content under dynamic network conditions. In this paper, we present FlexiView, a novel algorithm that jointly optimizes video quality and playout rate by leveraging chunk-specific characteristics, i.e., data size, SSIM, and VMAF, within edge-assisted video streaming environments. FlexiView employs Lyapunov-based and convex optimization techniques to dynamically adapt both parameters in real time, aiming to maximize user Quality of Experience (QoE), reduce video stalls, and stabilize fluctuations in video quality and playout rate. Extensive trace-driven simulations demonstrate that FlexiView outperforms existing adaptive bitrate and playout control algorithms by effectively balancing QoE enhancement, stall prevention, and system consistency.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Robust Ensemble-based Log Anomaly Detection for Securing Mobile Systems.
abstract: Modern mobile systems span smartphones, IoT devices, and edge nodes, evolving rapidly through frequent updates that expand their attack surface. These environments generate massive logs containing subtle security signals, such as mobile malware, rogue apps, insecure APIs, and compromised edge devices. Effective log anomaly detection (LAD) is therefore critical but challenging. Rule-based approaches and shallow models fail to generalize, while deep learning methods, though better at capturing log sequences, often suffer from high variance and fragile thresholding at scale, limiting their reliability for real-world mobile system security monitoring. To address the challenges, our core contribution is REMLog, a Robust Ensemble-based LAD framework designed to secure mobile systems. It unifies heterogeneous operational logs, from cloud control planes to sensor management platforms and mobile edge devices, into a single pipeline for scalable and reliable anomaly detection in complex mobile systems. To support high-volume log ingestion and lowlatency streaming analysis, REMLog integrates Apache Kafka as its ingestion backbone. Fundamentally, REMLog employs BAT, a bagging-based ensemble of EM-AT (Expectation Maximization-Anomaly Transformer) models with diversified parameterizations to significantly reduce decision variance and improve detection robustness. To address the difficulties of threshold sensitivity and manual calibration, we hereby implement EM-AT, an enhanced AT that integrates an EM procedure to automatically calibrate anomaly thresholds without manual tuning. In dynamic mobile environments, this allows the LAD model to adapt to varying noise profiles across diverse nodes. We evaluate REMLog on two widely used system log datasets, HDFS and OpenStack, which emulate realistic back-end infrastructures powering mobile and sensor service platforms. EM-AT achieves $F_{1}$-scores of $98.90 \%$ and 99.61 % on HDFS and OpenStack, respectively, while REMLog further improves performance to $99.99 \%$ on both datasets. These results show that REMLog delivers accurate, scalable, and robust LAD suitable for proactive security monitoring in mobile systems.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: Recogneech: A Phoneme Level CSI Sensing Framework for Silent Speech Recognition.
abstract: Silent speech recognition using WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) offers strong privacy benefits, but existing CSI-based efforts remain limited to word-level modeling. We present Recogneech, a phoneme-level CSI-based silent speech system that captures fine articulatory motions using a multidomain CSI pipeline and a 3D-ResNet backbone. A confidencegated refinement module resolves ambiguous phonemes through an XGBoost classifier. Experiments on a multi-user dataset of eight phoneme classes show that Recogneech achieves $94.81 \%$ accuracy and substantially reduces confusion in difficult vowel pairs, while maintaining robustness across users, distances, and behavioral variations. Our results demonstrate that phonemelevel articulatory patterns are distinguishable in CSI, enabling open-vocabulary silent speech on commodity WiFi devices.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Repairing LoRa Packets with Demodulated Symbols from Multiple Gateways by Exploiting the Block Structure of Codeword and Symbols.
abstract: LoRa has become one of the most prominent wireless technologies to connect IoT devices to gateways over long distances. In this paper, we propose a novel method referred to as Codeword Column Set Check (CCSC), which repairs corrupted LoRa packets when the packets are received by multiple gateways. One key advantage of CCSC is that the gateways only need to upload demodulated symbol which is around 10 bits per symbol, resulting in very low communication overhead. CCSC is based on a special block structure of LoRa that organizes codeword and symbols in a matrix. CCSC uses a simple method to identify correct copies of transmitted symbols and use them to correct other symbols. We mathematically prove that CCSC is optimal in the sense that it can repair all blocks that are theoretically repairable. We evaluate CCSC with both real-world experiments and simulations. We show that CCSC achieves $93 \%$ the performance of the best method that uploads physical layer signals while consuming negligible upload bandwidth of the latter. We also show that the gain of CCSC over the existing method with similar upload bandwidth consumption is $3 \times$.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: LightRider: Reliable UAV Ground Communication with a Single Laser Tethering Link.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly vulnerable to electromagnetic interference (EMI) in their communication and networking systems, posing significant risks to mission success and operational safety. To address the limitations of radio frequency ($\mathbf{R F}$) communication in such scenarios, we propose a reliable laser-based communication system for UAV operations in EMI-prone environments. Our system features a single laser tethering link (i.e., ensuring the laser beam continuously illuminates a moving UAV) that simultaneously enables laser tracking, alignment, and communication. Leveraging the optical properties of laser beams and retroreflectors, the laser tethering design utilizes a photodiode (PD) array to detect and calculate the precise position of the beam spot from a distance. We further design a beam alignment control algorithm that maintains continuous optical tethering using only the single, narrow laser beam. Our design effectively eliminates the need for RF-based position feedback (as conventional tethering design needed) that could be vulnerable to EMI interference. To minimize the interference between tethering and communication functions, we further design a beam spot prediction algorithm coupled with modulation, which compensates for the inevitable impact of modulation on the continuity of tethering.
