Experimental evaluation using our prototype demonstrates a maximum tethering distance of 150 meters and communication distances of 380 meters. The system successfully tracks UAVs moving at angular velocities up to $57^{\circ} / \mathrm{s}$ and maintains functionality in the presence of commercial UAV jammers. A demonstration video showcasing the system’s operation is available at https://youtu.be/rAFIpUadkOc.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Octopus: An ABR-RAN Closed-Loop Approach Towards High QoE Multi-User 5G VR Gaming.
abstract: The synergy between 5G and Virtual Reality is transforming the entertainment landscape, with Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) offering a flexible architecture for private 5G deployments. This paper introduces a comprehensive testbed to analyze Multi-User VR (MUVR) gaming performance over O-RAN. We identify three key factors that severely degrade the end-user Quality of Experience (QoE): prolonged tail latency, uneven bandwidth allocation, and unfair video quality. To address these problems, we present Octopus, a real-time interactive streaming system designed for MUVR over O-RAN. Octopus implements a bidirectional coordination mechanism that closes the loop between Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) streaming and RAN scheduling. By leveraging the O-RAN RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) framework, the system achieves cross-layer optimization while maintaining architectural flexibility. Experimental results demonstrate that Octopus significantly outperforms state-of-the-art VR streaming solutions, reducing the 99.99th percentile latency by $48.45 \%$, increasing average bitrate by $23.60 \%$, and improving streaming smoothness and max-min fairness by $63.16 \%$ and $104.34 \%$, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Packet-Level DDoS Data Augmentation Using Dual-Stream Temporal-Field Diffusion.
abstract: In response to Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, recent research efforts increasingly rely on Machine Learning (ML)-based solutions, whose effectiveness largely depends on the quality of labeled training datasets. To address the scarcity of such datasets, data augmentation with synthetic traces is often employed. However, current synthetic trace generation methods struggle to capture the complex temporal patterns and spatial distributions exhibited in emerging DDoS attacks. This results in insufficient resemblance to real traces and unsatisfied detection accuracy when applied to ML tasks. In this paper, we propose Dual-Stream Temporal-Field Diffusion (DSTF-Diffusion), a multi-view, multi-stream network traffic generative model based on diffusion models, featuring two main streams: The field stream utilizes spatial mapping to bridge network data characteristics with pre-trained realms of stable diffusion models, effectively translating complex network interactions into formats that stable diffusion can process, while the spatial stream adopts a dynamic temporal modeling approach, meticulously capturing the intrinsic temporal patterns of network traffic. Extensive experiments demonstrate that data generated by our model exhibits higher statistical similarity to originals compared to current state-of-the-art solutions, and enhance performances on a wide range of downstream tasks.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: PDE-TSN: Enable TSN Autonomous Self-healing under Link Faults.
abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) is an advanced real-time Ethernet technology that provides deterministic transmission through precise traffic scheduling. To ensure reliability in safety-critical applications under link faults, TSN introduces Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability (FRER) at the cost of significant bandwidth overhead. Moreover, most FRER implementations rely on statically configured redundant paths, which degrade the reliability under link faults, highlighting the need for dynamic fault recovery solutions. However, existing solutions fail to provide a system-level fault recovery capability, leaving TSN dependent on manual recovery with unacceptable recovery times.To address these challenges, this paper proposes PDE-TSN, an autonomous self-healing TSN solution that integrates link fault perception, scheduling decision, and reconfiguration execution in a closed loop. To support efficient runtime management, PDE-TSN leverages a lightweight management protocol, enabling timely fault reporting and online configuration deployment. In addition, a 3R-Driven scheduling algorithm is proposed, ensuring high reliability with low bandwidth overhead. Results using FPGA prototypes demonstrate that compared to FRER-only implementations under critical link faults, PDE-TSN achieves fast recovery (within 0.4 seconds per flow) to restore reliability for service continuity, while reducing bandwidth overhead by 40% at matched reliability.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Reliability-Aware Analysis of MIMO Cellular Networks via SIR Meta Distribution.
abstract: We develop an analytical framework for studying the meta distribution of the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) in wireless networks employing multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technologies. Specifically, we focus on the downlink of a cellular network where base stations (BSs) are spatially deployed according to a homogeneous Poisson point process. Each BS is equipped with multiple antennas and uses maximal ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming for data packet delivery. We begin by analyzing the case where each BS has two antennas. For this setting, we derive an exact expression for the SIR meta distribution and further provide a tight approximation based on the Beta distribution. Consequently, we derive expressions for several performance metrics, including the transmission success probability and the mean local delay in two-antenna cellular networks. For networks in which BSs are equipped with an arbitrary number of antennas, we derive an analytical expression for the SIR meta distribution, where the numerical value can be recursively calculated. We also develop a tractable approximation method to evaluate the meta distribution in this case. We conduct extensive simulations to validate the accuracy of our theoretical derivations and use the numerical results to illustrate the performance improvements enabled by increasing the number of antennas.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Enabling Reliable and Real-Time Packet Reception in User-Defined Overlapping LoRa Channels.
abstract: In LoRaWAN, users are allowed to customize the center frequency of channel. This mechanism provides more flexibility but also introduces non-negligible interference for packet reception. This paper focuses on Overlapping Channel Interference (OCI), which arises when multiple users simultaneously transmit on partially overlapping channels. Existing methods proposed for interference in a single channel concurrently demodulate collided packets by inferring the chirp’s onset and offset times. However, the collided chirps in OCI exhibit different center frequencies, leading to unpredictable chirp’s onset and offset times which makes OCI particularly challenging to resolve. To resolve it, we propose Hole, a novel method to reliably receive target packet by exploiting the difference in chirp’s onset and offset times instead of inferring them. Hole adopts signal elimination to construct identifiable energy losses for different chirps. Since the onset and offset times of target chirp are stable, its energy loss is deterministic while that of the interfering chirp is random. By comparing energy loss, we identify target chirp under OCI. However, in practice, the channel noise reduces the stability of energy loss. Therefore, we first theoretically analyze the optimal position of signal elimination and then propose noiseaware elimination setting. Furthermore, we also propose target packet recognition method by leveraging difference in packet’s center frequency offset. The experiments in real LoRa network present that Hole improves the Packet Reception Rate (PRR) by up to $7.5 \times$ compared with existing methods.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: RIScatter: Enhancing Backscatter Communication via Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces.
abstract: Backscatter communication is an attractive approach for battery-free Internet of Things, yet its practical deployment is often limited by severe attenuation across both the forward link and the backscatter link, as well as by environmental blockage. Although reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) offer a promising way to improve both hops through passive beamforming, existing RIS-assisted backscatter studies typically rely on explicit channel state information or dedicated training procedures that are unavailable for passive tags. In this paper, we present RIScatter, an end-to-end RIS-assisted backscatter system compatible with commodity BLE receivers. RIScatter addresses two core challenges: passive direction discovery and joint forward/backscatter configuration. For passive direction discovery, RIScatter uses infrastructure-side sensing based on global phase probing to extract a directional prior of the passive tag. For joint configuration, RIScatter constructs a compact dual-anchor codebook and performs RSSI-based online alignment over the resulting candidate set. We implement RIScatter with a 2-bit $16 \times 16$ RIS prototype and an FPGA-based BLE backscatter tag prototype. Experiments in indoor environments show that RIScatter substantially improves link reliability and usable range, reducing the bit error rate by $54 \times$ and extending the usable communication range to $4.2 \times$ that of the baseline without RIS.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Improving LPWAN Concurrency with Collision-Resilient Zadoff-Chu Random Access.
abstract: Low-Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs) support large-scale IoT connectivity but are capacity-limited, motivating concurrent transmissions to improve spectral efficiency. However, existing concurrent LPWAN solutions typically rely on a single base waveform or quasi-orthogonal waveforms, resulting in limited concurrency. In this paper, we propose Zadoff-Chu Random Access (ZCRA), a low-overhead framework for massive random access. ZCRA introduces a Zadoff-Chu-sequence-based waveform, which modulates multiple bits via cyclic shifts of Zadoff-Chu root sequences, exploiting their zero cyclic autocorrelation property. By allowing users to randomly select root sequences, ZCRA effectively mitigates inter-user interference without waveform pre-assignment based on low cross-correlation property. To resolve same-root collisions under low SINR, we further develop a constellation-set-match-based decoding scheme (CSMatch) that leverages spectral correlation structure to separate superimposed transmissions and remains robust to carrier frequency offsets and multipath channels. Extensive evaluation demonstrates that ZCRA-CSMatch significantly improves concurrency, achieving a lower symbol error rate compared with state-of-the-art collision resolution approaches, along with a $\mathbf{2. 1 3} \boldsymbol{\times}$ network throughput improvement over current concurrent systems and supporting 200 nodes (40 concurrency).
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Emotion-Aware Personalization: Resonating Short-Video Recommendations via Multi-Modal Affective Computing.
abstract: Modern short-video recommendation systems primarily rely on user-video interactions (e.g., sharing, rating, commenting) while neglecting nuanced emotional states, resulting in superficial engagement. To address this gap, we introduce MARS, an emotion-aware framework that dynamically aligns recommendations with viewers’ real-time affective states. We present two key contributions: First, leveraging multi-modal affective computing, MARS employs physiological signals from consumer-grade wearable biosensors (headphones, smartwatches, smartphones) to infer emotional context. Second, an emotion-aware graph convolutional network (EA-GCN) maps emotional trajectories continuously captured during viewing into a new edge embedding, enabling precise emotion-matched recommendations. This dual approach fosters adaptive personalization tailored to users’ evolving emotional needs. We validate MARS through a comprehensive study involving 70 participants and 30,000 user-video interactions. Results demonstrate $\mathbf{8 5 . 5 4 \%}$ classification accuracy in the circumplex settings, and $30.6 \%$ improvement in recommendation quality over state-of-the-art baselines. Our work advances affective computing in recommender systems by bridging psychological models with scalable machine-learning pipelines, offering a robust framework for emotionally intelligent personalization.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Poster: Automated Extraction of Protocol State Machines from 3GPP Specifications with Domain-Informed Prompts and LLM Ensembles.
abstract: Mobile telecommunication networks are foundational to global infrastructure and increasingly support critical sectors such as manufacturing, transportation, and healthcare. The security and reliability of these networks are essential, yet depend heavily on accurate modeling of underlying protocols through state machines. While most prior work constructs such models manually from 3GPP specifications, this process is labor-intensive, error-prone, and difficult to maintain due to the complexity and frequent updates of the specifications. Recent efforts using natural language processing have shown promise, but remain limited in handling the scale and intricacy of cellular protocols. In this work, we propose SpecGPT, a novel framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to automatically extract protocol state machines from 3 GPP documents. SpecGPT segments specifications into semantically meaningful paragraphs and constructs domain-informed prompts to guide model interpretation. We evaluate SpecGPT on three representative 5 G protocols (NAS, NGAP, and PFCP) using manually annotated ground truth, and show that it outperforms existing approaches, demonstrating the effectiveness of LLMs for protocol modeling at scale.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: AdSeeker: An Agent-Driven Framework for Automated Malicious Ad Detection in Mobile Apps.
abstract: Online advertisements (ads) play a critical role in sustaining the mobile ecosystem. However, imperfect ad review mechanisms allow ads to be exploited as a channel for malicious content dissemination, posing significant security risks to users and platforms. Existing malicious advertisement detection methods heavily rely on manually crafted rules, which limit automation and undermine detection robustness in complex and dynamic environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes AdSeeker, an automated malicious ad detection framework driven by an autonomous agent. AdSeeker leverages the agent’s decision-making capability to systematically explore application interfaces and collect multi-dimensional ad-related evidence, including ad SDK metadata, permission usage, network redirection links, and ad image elements. Based on the collected evidence, AdSeeker classifies malicious ad behaviors, assesses risk levels, and provides remediation suggestions, enabling quantitative security evaluation of mobile applications. We evaluate AdSeeker on 30,000 applications from AndroZoo. The results show that 10,497 apps contain ads, from which 14,971 ad samples are collected, including 1,537 malicious ads. AdSeeker achieves a detection precision of 96.30%. Our findings further reveal that malicious ads are present even in legitimate applications, highlighting the necessity for strengthened ad network auditing and more effective malicious ad governance to foster a safer mobile ecosystem. The source code is publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/AnaY1115/AdSeeker.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: MUND: Role-Aware Multi-Agent Learning for Dynamic UAV Network Deployment.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm networks have emerged as a powerful platform for supporting dynamic and complex applications such as disaster monitoring and moving target tracking. Nevertheless, effective coordination in large-scale UAV swarms remains challenging due to dynamically varying UAV roles, tightly coupled trajectory planning and network access decisions, as well as partial observability-induced scalability constraints. To address these challenges, this paper proposes MUND, a scalable multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) framework for dynamic UAV network deployment. MUND adopts a generalized system modeling approach suitable for large-scale environments and introduces a scalable role-aware learning framework that enables adaptive grouping and information sharing under partial observability. Furthermore, a structured reward decomposition strategy is designed to align individual UAV behaviors with global task completion and network quality objectives, effectively addressing the credit assignment problem under partial observability. Extensive experiments show that MUND significantly outperforms existing baselines, improving network deployment quality by $69.2 \%$ and boosting task-user data rates by $\mathbf{1 3 9 . 8 \%}$, demonstrating robust scalability and coordination efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: SmartCCL: Learn to Schedule Near-Optimal Collective Communication for GPU Clusters.
abstract: Efficient scheduling of the ALLGATHER collective communication primitive is critical for accelerating large-scale distributed training of deep learning models, yet its inherent NPhardness due to MILP modeling presents major bottlenecks in both solving efficiency and scalability. To address this, we propose SmartCCL, a novel two-stage scheduling framework combining Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with lightweight centralized greedy refinement. SmartCCL employs attentionbased deep neural networks within DRL agents to effectively capture dynamic network topology and global data distribution states, enabling intelligent, near-optimal forwarding decisions. Simulations under representative GPU cluster topologies NDv2 and DGX2 demonstrate that SmartCCL achieves over $\mathbf{9 0} \%$ of the optimal schedule performance compared to advanced MILP solvers, yet dramatically reduces solution generation time from hours to seconds. Moreover, its superior balance among scalability, solving efficiency, and solution quality significantly surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods, highlighting its strong practicality for real-world deployment.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: AdaptTree: A Practical and Adaptive Packet Classification Scheme on FPGA.
abstract: Packet classification is fundamental to various network functions such as access control and intrusion detection. While FPGAs offer high-throughput processing, existing designs suffer from two major challenges: limited scalability due to constrained on-chip memory, and poor flexibility as switching between diverse rule-sets often requires costly hardware reconfiguration.To address these challenges, we propose a novel decision tree scheme, AdaptTree, a practical FPGA-based packet classifier that significantly improves memory efficiency and architectural flexibility. To enhance scalability, AdaptTree adopts a hashing-based indexing scheme that eliminates pointer storage in inner nodes, reducing memory overhead. In addition, a novel skewed kicking strategy concentrates most rules into first few trees, mitigating memory fragmentation across multiple trees. To enable flexibility, AdaptTree incorporates a novel pipelined hardware architecture inspired by the concept of “empty operation”, allowing uniform storage of nodes and rules across pipeline stages. This design supports diverse rule-set mappings without requiring hardware reconfiguration.Evaluations show that AdaptTree achieves over 290 MPPS throughput, classifies 100 K -scale rule-sets using only 4.5 MB of on-chip memory, and supports fast rule updates and ruleset switching without compromising deterministic latency and ordered output-offering a scalable and flexible solution for realworld deployment.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Enabling Seamless LoRa-to-Mobile Bridging via Wi-Fi Spectrum Scanning.
abstract: LoRa is a popular low-power wireless technology in the Internet of Things (IoT), but direct interaction with consumer devices is hindered by protocol incompatibility. Existing crosstechnology communication (CTC) solutions for Wi-Fi receivers often require additional gateways or transmitters. We propose a LoRa-to-Wi-Fi CTC technique that enables smartphones to directly receive and decode LoRa transmissions using only their native hardware capabilities. Our key innovation is utilizing the spectrum scanning functionality in commercial mobile Wi-Fi chipsets for LoRa packet decoding. A signal processing pipeline combining frequency-domain analysis and lightweight neural-network-based symbol classification reliably recovers LoRa packets under commodity hardware constraints. Our prototype, implemented on a Google Pixel 5, demonstrates robust one-to-one LoRa-to-Wi-Fi communication with commercial LoRa tags, enabling smartphones to act as ad hoc LoRa listeners and simplifying infrastructure-free IoT data collection.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: Structure-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Energy-Constrained Background Update Scheduling.
abstract: Frequent background updates in mobile applications help maintain content freshness, but can lead to unnecessary energy consumption, especially when updates are discarded before user access. This paper studies the problem of scheduling background updates under an energy budget while accounting for stochastic user launch behavior. We formulate the problem as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) that minimizes user inconvenience subject to a long-term energy constraint. Analyzing the Lagrangian-relaxed MDP, we characterize the optimal policy as having a monotone threshold structure with respect to the update interval. Building on this structure, we propose SA-Q, a threshold-guided Q-learning algorithm that uses an online learned threshold to actively steer exploration toward informative regions and empirically reduce wasted sampling in constrained settings. This mechanism accelerates convergence and reduces training variance. Extensive simulations across diverse scenarios and real-world traces demonstrate that SA-Q consistently outperforms baseline methods, achieving up to $8.6 \%$ lower energy consumption while maintaining the same level of user experience.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: OFLight: Lightweight Gradient Compression for Over-the-Air Federated Learning.
abstract: Integrating over-the-air (OTA) computations into the model aggregation process of federated learning (FL) is an effective approach to alleviate the communication bottleneck in FL model training. Under this scheme, all the clients modulate their intermediate parameters, such as gradients, onto the same set of orthogonal waveforms and transmit the resultant signals to the edge server simultaneously. Capitalizing on the superposition property of multiple access channels, the server can extract an automatically aggregated global gradient from the received radio signal. However, the limited number of orthogonal waveforms hinders the use of more advanced, but high-dimensional models. In light of this challenge, we propose OFLight, a lightweight, yet effective, gradient compression algorithm for OTA FL systems. Specifically, in every communication round, the edge server uses the received gradient matrix to construct a low-rank matrix comprising the projection matrix and broadcasts it, along with the global model, to all clients in the system. Based on this matrix, every client projects its locally renewed gradient matrix into a low-dimensional subspace through a linear operation. The clients upload only their compressed gradients via OTA computations, and the edge server can perform a linear decompression on the received signal, retrieving the original gradient dimension. Moreover, to mitigate compression errors, an error feedback mechanism is incorporated. We derive analytical expressions for the convergence rate, quantitatively demonstrating the effect of OFLight on training efficiency. We also conduct extensive experiments to corroborate the efficacy of the proposed method.
conference_title: IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication, and Networking

title: 6Hunter: An Efficient Framework for Discovering Router Interfaces in IPv6 Network.
abstract: Discovering IPv6 router interfaces is crucial for network asset visibility and threat detection. However, existing technologies primarily focus on identifying address regions with a higher likelihood of yielding responses, generating / $\mathbf{6 4}$ prefixes within these regions as scanning targets while neglecting the utilization of existing active $/ 64$ prefixes. To address this gap, this paper proposes 6Hunter, an efficient IPv6 router interface discovery framework. 6Hunter performs pattern mining on known / 64 prefixes, generates / 64 prefixes as scanning targets based on the prefix patterns, and adopts a budget allocation method based on Bayesian smoothing mechanism for dynamic scanning. Experimental results demonstrate that with a budget of 100 million packets, 6Hunter outperforms Sweeper, Treestrace, FlashRoute, Yarrp6, and Scamper, achieving improvements of $\mathbf{1 2 0. 5 \% - 2 7 2 \%}$ in IPv6 address hit rate and $\mathbf{1 4 9 \% - 1 5 6. 1 \%}$ in IPv6 address discovery speed, respectively. Additionally, analysis of interface identifiers and ports of these IPv6 addresses indicates that a significant proportion of the discovered routers still face security vulnerabilities arising from privacy leakage and open ports.
